In step 4, I'm going to investigate the clusters identified by the clustering algorithm.  
 - How similar or dissimilar are they with respect to the primary topics (and the fields and subfields to which those topics belong) 
 - What are the most important works for each cluster based on page rank and betweenness.
 
To simplify this process, 
 
Workflow:
Step 1)  Add attributes in the node-list for the network characteristics:  cluster membership, page rank, and betweenness metrics.

Step 2) Explore the new node-list.
  
  a) overall descriptions of works (journal source, source group)
  b) group by cluster and summarize to compare average page rank and betweenness
  c) for each cluster, look at the primary_topic variables ==> FOR LOOP!!
  
Step 3) extract the most important works

To Recap:

I filtered the "works" to JUST those with NAIS-themed keywords in their title or primary_topic variables.  I found the "refs" that matched those work_ids to produce two edgelists:  
  * 1) the "open" edgelist includes NAIS-themed works that appear in EITHER the "citing" ("from") OR "cited" ("to") columns of the "refs" object. That means they could be citing or cited by works that do NOT have NAIS-themed titles or primary-topics.  
  
  * 2) the "insular" edgelist includes NAIS-themed works that were in BOTH the "citing" AND the "cited" columns of the refs object.  
  
Based on the unique references in the edgelist, I generated a nodelist by filtering the "works" to just those that appear in the edgelist.

Using the edgelist, I created a citation network and ran the Louvain clustering algorithm to identify clusters.  

The citation graph I'm starting with here "indig_clus_open" includes node modularity and betweenness centrality values, cluster membership, and 2 ranked measures of citation importance (page rank and grank).  

Here I want to link the citation graph to the nodelist and then explore the combined dataset: descriptive statistics and network visualizations that display some of the node attributes.


Step 1)  Add attributes in the node-list for the network characteristics:  cluster membership, page rank, and betweenness metrics.
       
       
```{r 1.1) add network attributes to node-list for open network}

# this line is essentially copy-pasted from Liza's code
# adds cluster number to each work

met$cluster <- V(cit_graph)$louv_cluster[match(met$work_id,V(cit_graph)$name)]

table(met$cluster)

# also want to find the works with the highest page rank and betweenness metrics

met$prank <- V(cit_graph)$prank[match(met$work_id,V(cit_graph)$name)]
met$btw <- V(cit_graph)$betweenness[match(met$work_id,V(cit_graph)$name)]
met$hi_btw <- V(cit_graph)$high_between[match(met$work_id,V(cit_graph)$name)]
met$highest <- V(cit_graph)$highest_in_group[match(met$work_id,V(cit_graph)$name)]

# really don't need some of these original columns

met_open <- met %>% 
   filter(!is.na(cluster)) %>% 
   select(-has_fulltext, -oa_is_oa, -oa_status)


# class(met_full)  # [1] "data.table" "data.frame"
# typeof(met_full)  # [1] "list"

saveRDS(met_open, "data/4a.1_indig_open_nodelist.rds")
# met_open <- readRDS(file = "data/4a.1_indig_open_nodelist.rds")

```


```{r 1.2) add network attributes to node-list for insular network}

# this line is essentially copy-pasted from Liza's code
# adds cluster number to each work

met2$cluster <- V(cit_graph2)$louv_cluster[match(met2$work_id,V(cit_graph2)$name)]

table(met2$cluster)

# also want to find the works with the highest page rank and betweenness metrics

met2$prank <- V(cit_graph2)$prank[match(met2$work_id,V(cit_graph2)$name)]
met2$btw <- V(cit_graph2)$betweenness[match(met2$work_id,V(cit_graph2)$name)]
met2$hi_btw <- V(cit_graph2)$high_between[match(met2$work_id,V(cit_graph2)$name)]
met2$highest <- V(cit_graph2)$highest_in_group[match(met2$work_id,V(cit_graph2)$name)]

# really don't need some of these original columns

met_insular <- met2 %>% 
  filter(!is.na(cluster)) |> 
  select(-has_fulltext, -oa_is_oa, -oa_status)

# class(met_insular)  # [1] "data.table" "data.frame"
# typeof(met_insular)  # [1] "list"

saveRDS(met_insular, "data/4a.2_indig_insular_nodelist.rds")
# readRDS(file = "data/4a.2_indig_insular_nodelist.rds")

```
